quickSummary: Glycosidic bonds join sugars via dehydration. Maltose (α-1,4) and Lactose (β-1,4) are reducing sugars; Sucrose (α,β-1,2) is non-reducing because both anomeric carbons are locked. Starch contains unbranched helical Amylose (traps I2 for blue-black color) and branched Amylopectin (α-1,4 and α-1,6). Glycogen is animal starch with frequent α-1,6 branches. Cellulose has unbranched linear β-1,4 chains (negative iodine test). Chitin is a NAG polymer; Inulin is a fructose polymer used to measure GFR.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 Glycosidic Linkages & Disaccharide Properties
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 Glycosidic Linkages & Disaccharide Properties

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Maltose & Lactose = Reducing. Sucrose = Non-reducing (anomeric C1 and C2 locked in α,β-1,2 bond). Starch amylose traps iodine; cellulose does NOT.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DISACCHARIDE LINKAGE ARCHITECTURE
                        
   MALTOSE:  $\alpha$-$\text{D}$-Glucose + $\alpha$-$\text{D}$-Glucose   ──► $\alpha$-(1 $\rightarrow$ 4) Glycosidic Bond (Reducing)
   LACTOSE:  $\beta$-$\text{D}$-Galactose + $\beta$-$\text{D}$-Glucose  ──► $\beta$-(1 $\rightarrow$ 4) Glycosidic Bond (Reducing)
   SUCROSE:  $\alpha$-$\text{D}$-Glucose + $\beta$-$\text{D}$-Fructose  ──► $\alpha$,$\beta$-(1 $\rightarrow$ 2) Glycosidic Bond (NON-REDUCING)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Reducing Sugars**: Possess a free anomeric aldehyde or ketone group capable of reducing alkaline cupric ions ($\text{Cu}^{2+}$) to red cuprous oxide ($\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$) precipitate in Benedict's and Fehling's tests (*e.g., all monosaccharides, Maltose, Lactose, Cellobiose*).
• **Non-Reducing Sugars**: Both anomeric carbons are locked inside the glycosidic bond (*e.g., Sucrose, Trehalose*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.3 Polysaccharide Chemistry & Structural Diversity
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.3 Polysaccharide Chemistry & Structural Diversity
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HOMOPOLYSACCHARIDE STRUCTURAL DIVERSITY
                                         │
         ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                               ▼                               ▼
      STARCH                          GLYCOGEN                        CELLULOSE
 (Storage in Plants)             (Storage in Animals/Fungi)       (Structural Plant Walls)
 ├── Amylose (Linear $\alpha$-1,4) ├── Hyper-branched $\alpha$-1,4       └── Unbranched Linear $\beta$-1,4
 └── Amylopectin (Branched          with $\alpha$-1,6 branch points       glucan chains (H-bonded
     $\alpha$-1,4 & $\alpha$-1,6)       every 8–12 glucose units          microfibril sheets)
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Starch (Plant Storage)**:
   - **Amylose (15–20%)**: Unbranched linear chain with $\alpha$-(1 $\rightarrow$ 4) bonds. Forms a secondary helical coil that traps iodine ($\text{I}_2$) molecules inside its lumen to produce a **deep blue-black color**.
   - **Amylopectin (80–85%)**: Branched polymer with $\alpha$-(1 $\rightarrow$ 4) linear chains and $\alpha$-(1 $\rightarrow$ 6) branch points every 24–30 glucose residues.
2. **Glycogen ('Animal Starch')**: Highly branched storage polymer in liver and muscle. Features $\alpha$-(1 $\rightarrow$ 4) linear bonds and $\alpha$-(1 $\rightarrow$ 6) branch points every 8–12 glucose units (stains red-violet with iodine).
3. **Cellulose (Plant Cell Walls)**: Linear, unbranched structural homopolymer of $\beta$-$\text{D}$-glucose linked by $\beta$-(1 $\rightarrow$ 4) bonds. Parallel chains form rigid hydrogen-bonded microfibrils. *Lacks helical coils; gives a NEGATIVE iodine test*.
4. **Chitin**: Structural homopolymer of N-acetylglucosamine (NAG) linked by $\beta$-(1 $\rightarrow$ 4) bonds (arthropod exoskeletons and fungal walls).
5. **Inulin**: Linear storage homopolymer of fructose linked by $\beta$-(2 $\rightarrow$ 1) bonds (*Dahlia tubers*). Freely filtered by glomeruli without reabsorption; used to measure **Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)**.
